content.user_title: Audit Analytics Tracking for Decision-Ready Data
content.value_statement: Analytics teams often collect noisy events that do not support real decisions. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design, audit, and validate tracking systems.
actual_capabilities: Scores analytics readiness with a 0 to 100 measurement quality index.
Maps tracked events to business decisions and accountable users.
Designs event names, properties, triggers, and conversion rules.
Reviews GA4, GTM, UTM, and attribution practices for consistency.
Identifies common data quality issues, including duplicate events and PII leakage.
Produces measurement summaries, tracking plans, conversion tables, and validation notes.
limitations: Requires accurate context about tools, events, conversions, and business goals.
Does not connect to analytics platforms or deploy tags directly.
Does not replace hands-on QA in browsers, devices, and consent states.
Privacy and regulatory decisions may require legal or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Audit Product Analytics
use_cases.description: Review event quality, conversion definitions, and decision alignment before a roadmap planning cycle.

use_cases.title: Clean Marketing Attribution
use_cases.description: Standardize UTMs, campaign context, and conversion counting before evaluating channel performance.

use_cases.title: Prepare Tag Implementation
use_cases.description: Create a tracking plan with event names, properties, triggers, owners, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Current Tracking
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit for a small site or product.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this analytics tracking skill to assess my current setup. Ask for the minimum context you need, then score measurement readiness and list the top fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Tracking Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a new funnel.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tracking plan for a funnel with awareness, signup, activation, and purchase steps. Include event names, properties, triggers, and decisions supported.

prompt_templates.title: Validate GA4 and GTM Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my GA4 and GTM implementation plan. Check for duplicate firing, weak conversion definitions, missing properties, PII risk, and consent-state gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Measurement Governance Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced operating model for a growing team.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design governance for our analytics system. Define ownership, naming standards, version control, validation cadence, remediation order, and monitoring expectations.

output_examples.input: Audit a signup funnel with page views, button clicks, and signup completion events.
output_examples.output: Measurement readiness score: 68, unreliable. Main gaps are unclear conversion counting, duplicate CTA events, and missing attribution context. Fix conversions before optimization.

output_examples.input: Create a tracking plan for a product onboarding flow.
output: Track onboarding_started, onboarding_step_completed, feature_activated, and onboarding_completed.
Use properties for step name, plan, user type, and activation method.
Validate events in real time, mobile browsers, and consent-disabled sessions.

output_examples.input: Review UTM practices for paid campaigns.
output_examples.output: Use lowercase campaign values, documented separators, and one central source of truth. Prevent client-side overwrites and validate source preservation across domains.

best_practices: Start with business questions before adding events.
Keep event names consistent, specific, and tied to user intent.
Validate tracking across browsers, devices, consent states, and release changes.
anti_patterns: Tracking every click without a decision owner.
Treating GA4 numbers as truth before validating instrumentation.
Using free-text properties, PII, or inconsistent UTM formats.

faq.question: What analytics tools does this skill support?
faq.answer: It gives general measurement guidance and includes optional GA4, GTM, UTM, and attribution practices.

faq.question: Can it implement tags for me?
faq.answer: No. It creates plans, audits, and validation guidance, but it does not deploy analytics code or tags.

faq.question: When should I use the readiness score?
faq.answer: Use it before optimization, experimentation, reporting changes, or new tracking work.

faq.question: Does it handle privacy requirements?
faq.answer: It prompts for consent, data minimization, retention, and deletion considerations. Legal review may still be required.

faq.question: Can it reduce event sprawl?
faq.answer: Yes. It removes events that do not support decisions and focuses on meaningful state changes.

faq.question: Is it useful for product and marketing teams?
faq.answer: Yes. It connects events, conversions, attribution, and data quality to decisions across both teams.
